core_findings.claim: Camera setters operate on one Camera* / one camera render identifier, not a weapon domain.

Post-projection setter copies a64-byte matrix into a deferred camera command: envelope type2,size0x58; payload kind4,cameraID,matrix. It does not retain a readable matrix in the host Camera struct on this path.
Near/far/projection and frustum/FOV command types are distinct. Near/far/type host values are queued in type0 payload kind4; FOV/frustum values in type1 payload kind4.
Multiple viewports/render targets and render calls are implemented, but this does not prove a preexisting isolated viewmodel pass, per-weapon FOV or an acceptable composition/depth strategy.
Shader-pass flags are64-bit global-registry masks distinct from mesh byte visibility masks. Unknown flag names map to index-1, which register BTS/BTR masks to bit63.
Camera.set_mode and Application.update_render_world are literal no-op binding entrypoints on this image.
Post-projection calls alone cannot be declared safely restorable to the prior native matrix because the inspected setter has no host-side baseline/getter.
core_findings.status: baseline unavailable in inspected path; render-side baseline unknown

core_findings.claim: Mesh.visibility reads byte+0xdc and returns bit0 only; full-pass restoration still requires the guarded full byte or separately qualified per-pass observations.
